MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 27, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on August 27, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 22, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Vasquez

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Elaine Lister.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AMD RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 Mayor Kelly recessed to Closed Session. Mayor Kelley reconvened the meeting
at 6:01 p.m.
City Council Minutes  1  August 27, 2024
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that the City negotiators were given some direction and
parameters, but no reportable action was taken.

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim Mid-Summer Through Early Autumn 2024 as Wildfire Awareness &

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamation to Fire Chief Cheyne Maule.

P2. Recognize Mission Viejo Girls Softball League Teams 10U Silver Mayhem for Placing
  1st at USA Softball Regional Tournament and 14U Gold Adrenaline for Placing 1st at
  USA Softball SoCal State Tournament

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Pointed out the discrepancy of wording in the Impartial Analysis that was
changed due to her due diligence in pointing out to staff. Questioned where the oversight and
check and balances.

Ben Cartlidge, M.V.: Spoke on the Character Word of the Month “Self-Control”. Highlighted the
STAR Process which stands for Stop, Think, Act, Review, and gave examples of how he has
implemented this in his life.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Congratulated Elaine Lister on becoming City Manager and outlined how
the decision to appoint her was unanimous.

Sharon Genton, M.V.: Announced the Inaugural “Love Mission Viejo Day”, which will take place
on Saturday October 12 at Newhart Elementary School at 9 am. There will be various volunteer
projects and encouraged residents to attend. For more information residents can go to
www.lovemissionviejo.org

Cathleen Pryor, M.V.: Introduced herself as the President of the Laguna Heights Community
Association in Laguna Niguel. She voiced her concerns and wanted to alert the City of the
proposed lithium battery storage facility being proposed in San Juan that was denied a permit,
however they have appealed to the State which can override San Juans ordinance prohibiting this

City Council Minutes  2  August 27, 2024

residents.

PUBLIC HEARING

24. Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds
  on Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2024

  Public Services Manager Corey Gonyea presented the staff report.
City Council Minutes  5  August 27, 2024
   Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 6:58 pm.

  Victoria Bruno, M.V.: Objected to the proposed weed abatement due to the protection of
  trees and shrubs in open spaces, such as the coastal stage, scrub chaparral, and southern oak
  woodland.

  Mayor Kelley Closed the Public Hearing at 7:01 pm.

  Assistant City Manager Jerry Hill explained that the City works very closely with the OCFA
  staff in regard to any fire concerns related to weed abatement along with environmental
  biologists that we use in order to make sure we are preserving any native species.

  City Attorney Curley pointed out that this proposed weed abatement is for residential
  properties aimed at fire safety and aesthetics.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  Approve Instructed the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of
  weeds in accordance with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum and Vasquez

NEW BUSINESS

25. Consideration of Requesting Governor Newsom to Declare a State of Emergency as
  Regards the Present Property Insurance Crisis in the State of California

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, to adopt
  Resolution 24-42 Requesting the Governor of California to Declare a Statewide State of
  Emergency as to the Availability of Structure Fire Insurance for Residential, Commercial,
  and Industrial Structures in California.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum and Vasquez

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell stated that there will be a deeper dive report on the results from the trip
to the Olympic in Paris after they meet as a group. He did say that it was a very successful trip,
and the goal was met to sign a memorandum of understanding with Team Netherlands to make
this a training ground for the next Olympics. Council Member Goodell said they were wonderful
and people to engage with and we are looking forward to the same type of atmosphere here. They
met with other groups that are also looking for a home away from home during the Los Angeles
Olympics. He announced that the Nadadores Dive Team won the National Championship this year
and our Master Swim Team finished second place to San Diego Masters. He noted that the oldest
swimmers were 104, 94, 91 and 89 which was incredible to watch and a great event.

City Council Minutes  7  August 27, 2024
 Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch spoke on the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) Program. He explained
yesterday at Turf Park was the first release of approximately 4,400 radiated and marked male
mosquitoes to breed with female mosquitos which will produce sterile mosquitos. This should
drop the mosquito population, and it should make a difference. Overall, the next 36 days they will
be monitored to see how far they fly by the traps set throughout the area. Lastly, he shared a quote
from the athletic director of the Netherlands stating “There were other communities that they met
that had better facilities that would meet the Dutch needs, but they chose Mission Viejo because
of the friendliness of our community. It made them feel they were welcome here and that’s why
they are coming to Mission Viejo”. Mayor Pro Tem expressed that this is a great testament to who
we are and yes, we are an Olympic City and we now have the eighth most successful team in the
world coming to Mission Viejo.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley highlighted the following events she attended; Concert on the Green July 19, two
Night Markets, the Farmers Market, Boots Beer and Barbecue, Pacific Symphony and Prelude in
the Park, National Night Out Event, Library and Cultural Services Volunteer Recognition. She
also attended a photo opportunity with Congresswoman Young Kim and Santa Margarita Water
District at Lake Mission Viejo to highlight Congresswoman Kim for securing over a million
dollars in funding that would be use to help offset construction costs for the installation of the
Mission Viejo Brine Line Project which will allow Santa Margarita Water District and the
downstream Reclamation agencies the ability to produce a lot more recycled water, which helps
our lake and helps regional demands on imported portable water to South Orange County. She
stated she attended the Masters Swim Meet and was so surprised that 1300 swimmers competed
from all over the nation and the number of cars parked along Marguerite Parkway and adjacent
neighborhoods by the aquatics center. Lastly, she attended Paddle for the Battle Pickleball
Tournament at Felipe Tennis Center.
